title: SALAD porting gaps: parity, encoder training wiring, optimizer step
outcome: Fixed 5-site Rigid.__getitem__ crash class (encoder.py + losses/{structure,total}.py) blocking training entirely; wired real jointly-trained Encoder into prepare_batch (overfit confirms loss falls, params move, grad flows); training-step gradients match JAX (whole-model cosine 0.99999863, norm rel 1.07e-4) after isolating an unfixable cross-backend ADM-mask RNG source; transcribed reveal_conditioning exactly from NSB source (3 concrete fixes incl. previously-missing dssp_mean); default_vp_scaled/multimotif_vp forward parity measured (0.0059A / 0.037A) but not root-caused

title: Parity bisect: default_vp_scaled and multimotif_vp fixtures were TF32
outcome: Root cause of the 300x/1800x parity gap: both fixtures were generated on an H100 where XLA lowers float32 dot to TF32; regenerating default_vp (the config that always passed) on GPU reproduces the entire signature (out_pos 5.98e-03 A, block0 1.22e-02 A, aatype still 0/48). Per-block bisection (17 tensors x 6 blocks, both backends) shows torch matches CPU JAX to 9.27e-06 A with 0/3072 neighbour index differences. Fixed: jax_default_matmul_precision=highest pinned in the generator (bit-exact no-op on CPU), jax_platform/jax_matmul_precision recorded in every fixture, parity test refuses a non-fp32 fixture. All four configs now pass: 0.00002/0.00002/0.00002/0.00020 A. Refutes K013 and the N004 'it must be the weights' framing.

title: Fast preset: 40-design validation of the halved schedule
outcome: steps_scale=0.5 STAYS the fast default. At n=160/arm (40 seed-42 + 120 seed-1234) the halved schedule is indistinguishable from exact in mean (Welch all p>=0.24), spread (Brown-Forsythe, nothing survives Bonferroni over 18) and distribution shape (two-sample KS all p>=0.13). The feared less-SSE/more-extended direction is refuted WITH POWER (detectable 0.106 helix / 0.095 strand / 0.51 A Rg / 0.0041 A CA-CA vs largest observed 0.013 / 0.019 / 0.00 / 0.0015) and helix moves UP. n=40 would have got it wrong twice: N011 n=8 helix/Rg shift AND an n=40 Rg-spread at 2.3x exact off 3 designs were both noise. DIVERGED designs are the MODEL failure mode: 2/160 on exact (CA-CA 28.3 A, Rg 408 A), 0/160 on all three deviating arms, Fisher p=0.498. Code change is comment-only; gates byte-identical to unmodified HEAD (0.00002/0.00020 A, geometry 38/38, SUITE_EXIT=0).

title: Triton kernel audit: the 524 unaudited inductor kernels
HkLinear matmul lowering: batch-1 bmm -> mm/addmm + inductor matmul templates
outcome: mm/addmm lowering REJECTED (not bit-exact; addmm fails test_model_parity outright on multimotif_vp). Matmul templates alone (einsum unchanged, via inductor's tuned_bmm - refutes the 'batch-1 bmm forecloses templates' premise) are a real speedup but measured NOT bit-exact whole-forward under SALAD_OPT_DETSEG=1, and not reproducible against itself across cold-cache autotune compiles -> rejected from exact/deterministic (bit-exactness required) and from fast (no n=160 validation run) -> ships nowhere; SALAD_OPT_GEMMTPL stays opt-in-only default False. Fixed SALAD_OPT_MM default from the handoff's wrong 'mm' back to 'einsum'. Net shipped effect on the model: none. Full parity suite SUITE_EXIT=0 throughout, re-confirmed on the live git tree post-port (job 904659) alongside N021's concurrent uncommitted work in the same file.
